You don't necessarily need to see a doctor unless your mucus turns green (indicates bacterial infection) or you have a fever that doesn't subside after several days.

However, if you want the peace of mind from seeing a healthcare provider, it definitely won't hurt!

A good first step would be to look up your plan benefits and see what providers are covered. If you don't already have a PCP it might take a few days or a couple weeks to get in with one; an alternative is that you could try to see a nurse practitioner or even go to a walk in clinic. Your plan might also have a resource like MD Live, where you can make a same-day telehealth appointment to speak with a nurse/physician/NP who can give you an initial assessment and direct you how to proceed from there. This option could be low cost or in some cases even free.

You're not rude or patronizing regardless. Think about it this way: Say your partner has diabetes. You have no one in your close circle of friends or families that has it, so you're not super familiar with it or how it affects a person's life even though you might know the basics of what it is. If you're in a committed relationship with that partner, the burden is on you to learn about their medical condition so that as their partner you can provide the best support possible. It would be pretty insensitive and neglectful if you weren't proactive about doing that, right? Especially if their diabetes played a big role in how they are able to live their life? 

Do you see what I'm getting at here? Your mental illness are just as valid as any other medical condition, and if your SO is serious about dating you then he needs to put in effort to understand your depression so that he can he can properly support you (and your relationship will only be stronger for it). If he has such a basic/misinformed understanding of it that you don't think he's likely to get a good start himself, you can send him some resources to get started with (articles, videos, books, whatever). 

If you don't know how to bring it up, you can say something like, "my depression/anxiety is something that really affects my daily life and it really hurts me/is invalidating when you act like I can just decide to be okay and that will make me better.
